name: Pegataur
printedPages: DM’s Booklet pp. 3–5 and 23–24, including Table 8. pp. 6–8 and 26–27.
sourceDistinctions: Separate player-creature class from Centaur and Pegasus.
Shared Table 2 gives AC 6. The species chapter calls AC 5 natural and says to retain it even in inferior armor. The NPC follows that more specific text.
The original monster entry supplies ground speed and the option to attack with a pair of hooves. The NPC uses the PC2 spell progression and saves.

name: Sphinx
printedPages: DM’s Booklet pp. 3–5 and 25–27, including Table 9. pp. 6–8 and 28–30.
sourceDistinctions: Uses the playable PC2 progression. Rules Cyclopedia contributes ground movement and core attack/saving tables.
Table 9 gives AC 0 at the normal-monster tier, superseding general Table 2’s AC 2.
For the NPC’s 4-HD tier, Table 9 prints fear as 1d8 rounds, although the preceding prose groups that tier with 1d4 rounds. The build follows the explicit row.

name: Tabi
printedPages: DM’s Booklet pp. 3–5 and 28–30, including Tables 10–11. pp. 6–8 and 31–33.
sourceDistinctions: Separate from Phanaton and Gremlin. Creature Catalogue supplies land movement, while PC2 supplies the playable AC, venom and abilities.
The level-one row has 45%/50%/50% skills and one spell in the first level band. The corresponding normal-monster Hide in Shadows entry appears to have a missing zero.

name: Pterran
publication: Dark Sun Campaign Setting, Expanded and Revised (1995)
printedPages: The Age of Heroes pp. 7–8, 17–20, 42 and 54. pp. 139–140, 149–152, 174 and 186. The Way of the Psionicist pp. 18–19 (pp. 248–249).
sourceDistinctions: Uses the 1995 expanded and revised character profile. Separate from Saurial and the pterrax creature.

The metaplot and PC paths come from The Age of Heroes. The NPC uses a standard third-level fighter with no specialization. The book indicates many NPCs have a wild talent and leaves room for an NPC without one.
